name: add_tests_ruby_csv_normalizer
description: Asks the model to write Minitest tests for a CSV row normalizer; mutation-checked
prompts: RowNormalizer.normalize(row) in lib/row_normalizer.rb (already correct, do not modify it) takes a Hash with string keys "name", "email", and "age" and returns a cleaned Hash with symbol keys: :name is the value stripped of surrounding whitespace; :email is stripped AND downcased; :age is the value converted to an Integer, or nil if it is blank or not a valid integer. Write Minitest tests at exactly test/row_normalizer_test.rb (class RowNormalizerTest < Minitest::Test) with at least 4 test methods that pin this behavior precisely: that :name is trimmed, that :email is trimmed and lowercased, that a numeric :age string becomes the Integer, and that a blank or non-numeric :age becomes nil. Use assert_equal / assert_nil with exact expected values. Begin the file with `require "minitest/autorun"` and `require_relative "../lib/row_normalizer"`.

setup_files.lib/row_normalizer.rb:
module App
  class RowNormalizer
    # Normalize a raw CSV row (string keys) into a clean hash (symbol keys):
    # trim name; trim + downcase email; parse age to Integer or nil.
    def self.normalize(row)
      {
        name: row["name"].to_s.strip,
        email: row["email"].to_s.strip.downcase,
        age: Integer(row["age"].to_s.strip, exception: false),
      }
    end
  end
end

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("lib/row_normalizer.rb")
TEST_CMD = "ruby -Itest -Ilib test/row_normalizer_test.rb"
# Each mutant is a single-anchor replacement that breaks exactly one clause.
MUTANTS = [
    # name no longer trimmed
    ['name: row["name"].to_s.strip,', 'name: row["name"].to_s,'],
    # email no longer downcased
    ['email: row["email"].to_s.strip.downcase,', 'email: row["email"].to_s.strip,'],
    # age no longer parsed to Integer (left as the raw string)
    ['age: Integer(row["age"].to_s.strip, exception: false),', 'age: row["age"].to_s.strip,'],
]


def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode


src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for old, _new in MUTANTS:
    assert src.count(old) == 1, (
        f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to "
        f"change it (anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, (old, new) in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        IMPL.write_text(src.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately "
            f"broken implementation, so they do not verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print(f"PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {len(MUTANTS)} mutants)")

reference_solution.test/row_normalizer_test.rb:
require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/row_normalizer"

class RowNormalizerTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_name_is_trimmed
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "  Ada  ", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "30" })
    assert_equal "Ada", result[:name]
  end

  def test_email_is_trimmed_and_downcased
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "  Ada@Example.COM ", "age" => "30" })
    assert_equal "ada@example.com", result[:email]
  end

  def test_numeric_age_becomes_integer
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => " 42 " })
    assert_equal 42, result[:age]
  end

  def test_blank_or_bad_age_becomes_nil
    blank = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "  " })
    assert_nil blank[:age]
    bad = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "old" })
    assert_nil bad[:age]
  end
end

require "minitest/autorun"
require_relative "../lib/row_normalizer"

class RowNormalizerTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_returns_hash
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "30" })
    assert_kind_of Hash, result
  end

  def test_has_keys
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "30" })
    assert result.key?(:name)
    assert result.key?(:email)
    assert result.key?(:age)
  end

  def test_name_present
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "30" })
    refute_nil result[:name]
  end

  def test_age_kind
    result = App::RowNormalizer.normalize({ "name" => "Ada", "email" => "a@b.com", "age" => "30" })
    assert result[:age].is_a?(Integer) || result[:age].nil?
  end
end
